messages:
sahil: ran a focused nsys trace on the high-seqlen job (seq=2048, microbatch=1) and getting sustained HBM write bursts + long kernel gaps. attaching quick notes and timeline snippet. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

ida: can you paste the nsys command you used? also which kernel set (cutlass/flash-attn/custom) was active for the run?

sahil: command was: `nsys profile --output trace_hbm_kv --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx` around the load test. model used is our opt-30b variant with our new kv-page allocator and default kernel-dispatch policy (auto-kernel).

josh: quick q: microbatch=1 + seq=2048 means a lot of KV churn per request, especially if kv pages are sized for 1024. are you hitting the page-split code path?

sahil: yes, the allocator logs show repeated page splits. snippet from runtime logs: ```
[KVALLOC] page_alloc id=42 size=1.2MB -> created, owner=beam206
[KVALLOC] split page id=42 -> 42a(0.6MB),42b(0.6MB)
[KVACCESS] evict candidate count=8, hbm_pressure=0.89
[HBM] write_bytes=1.7GB/s read_bytes=0.2GB/s
```

maria: that HBM write skew is suspicious — writes >> reads. suggests we're materializing large KV pages out of L2/host or zeroing pages frequently. do you see any kernel that does memcpy (cudaMemcpyAsync) at those times?

perfbot: automated-nsys-insights: high HBM write throughput detected at 1995432118-1995432150, correlated with CPU->GPU memcpy spikes and long gaps (20-40ms) between attention kernels. Possible page thrash.

ida: can you share a small perfetto/trace viewer link? a kernel timeline screenshot helps.

sahil: uploaded timeline: https://perfetto.redwood/s/trace/1995432100/timeline (internal). timeline shows repeated pattern: small attention kernels (~2-3ms) then a 30-50ms blank gap where HBM writes dominate and then many kernels queue up.

josh: that pattern reads like synchronous page flush + kernel fallback. If the allocator takes a mutex and then issues host->device copies while holding the map, everything stalls. search for long CPU-side stacks around the copy events.

maria: also check our kernel-selection fallback: when seq > 1024 we sometimes switch kernels that touch KV in-place vs streaming. maybe the selected kernel forces materialization of KV into contiguous HBM. which kernel ID was chosen in trace?

sahil: tracer shows kernel id=0x4f (named attn_stream_merge) got picked repeatedly. looking at kernel metadata, it asserts `requires_contiguous_kv=true`. so it triggers a pre-copy step that compacts scattered KV pages into a contiguous buffer before launching.

aj: aha — that explains HBM writes. For large seqs, contiguous KV reduces kernel complexity but costs a copy. With microbatch=1 the copy isn't amortized. I'd try: 1) enable streaming kernel variant for >1024 that supports fragmented KV, or 2) increase microbatch to amortize copy cost, or 3) enable async copy + double-buffering so kernel queue isn't blocked.

ida: can we reproduce with a minimal harness? if yes, create an nsys with `--capture-range=thread:main` and `nvtxRangePush/Pop` around the allocator path so we can zoom exactly. Also add `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` and run with `--sample=none` to preserve timestamps.

sahil: repro harness planned. quick numbers from current trace: during the 32s run there were ~120 contiguous-copy ops totaling 65GB writes -> ~2GB/s sustained during spikes. CPU-side memcpy peaks at ~400MB/s per thread (we have 8 worker threads).

maria: another angle: kernel selection policy should look at microbatch and seq both. we currently pick by seq only. propose a heuristic: if microbatch <=2 and seq>1536 prefer 'fragmented-kv-stream' kernels or skip contiguous compaction. open to swapping default.

josh: +1. also add an internal metric: "kv_compaction_time" to the console per-route so we can see unit economics. if this compaction costs 30ms and tokens are 2000, that's expensive.

aj: i can prototype an asynchronous compaction patch: spawn a copy worker that posts cudaMemcpyAsync into a separate stream and uses cudaEvent to signal readiness. policy will launch kernel on compute stream if event recorded, else fall back to a streaming kernel that can operate on scattered pages. should eliminate long blank gaps.

perfbot: perfbot-suggest: recommended experiment — run A/B: (A) contiguous compaction synchronous, (B) async double-buffer + streaming fallback. Compare 95th latency and HBM write samples. perfbot will automatically tag traces if you name them with `kbw-exp-*` prefix.

sahil: plan: repro harness + two variants. I'll run both with nsys and share perfetto links + nsys csv. ETA end of day. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ida: Thanks — if you hit any weird CUDA driver stalls, ping me and I'll help dig nvprof counters (DRAM_ACTIVE_CYCLES etc).

maria: one last note: add a unit test that triggers page-split path to avoid regressions. we missed this pattern in the last rollout.

sahil: will do. creating follow-up issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-2047 (kv compaction async experiment).
